content.overview: A certificate of analysis is a structured report, not a free-standing truth label. The result must be connected to the correct sample, method, units and reporting conditions.

vocabulary.definition: Substance or property measured by an analytical procedure.
Method-specific threshold used to report or qualify a result.
Condition or denominator, such as mass basis, to which a result refers.

sections.title: Verify identity and scope first
sections.body: Laboratory, report number, sample ID, source lot, receipt and analysis dates, requested panel and authorization should agree.

sections.title: Method and units shape meaning
sections.body: Results using different preparation, method, basis or units may not be directly comparable even when analyte names match.

sections.title: Qualifiers are part of the result
sections.body: Reporting limits, uncertainty, deviations, dilution, matrix interference and amendments should be reviewed rather than stripped from the numeric value.

workedExamples: Two cannabinoid percentages differ, but one is reported on a different basis; unit conversion alone may not resolve method comparability.
commonMistakes: Comparing numbers without method and basis.
content.practicalApplication: Annotate a sample COA with identity checks, method, units, basis, qualifiers, limitations and questions requiring laboratory clarification.
content.summary: COA literacy means interpreting the complete report context, not extracting a number from its evidence chain.
